page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 144 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 72 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 540 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 3.75 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile operations.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core execution. While single-core performance on stress-ng falls in the average tier, multi-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier. The instance demonstrates high memory throughput, with cached read bandwidth reaching 11,548.62 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth at 213.92 GB/sec. Computational benchmarks such as Passmark CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores are positioned in the top 10% of tested systems. For LLM inference, the server exhibits top-tier prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large models, though text generation speeds for smaller models scale down to average levels.

Given its high core density and advanced matrix instruction support, this instance is suited for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based LLM inference. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the lack of bundled local storage and GPUs focuses the hardware profile purely on dense x86 compute and memory bandwidth. This makes it a resource-efficient option for highly parallelized, non-graphical enterprise workloads that require substantial multi-threaded processing power without the overhead of dedicated accelerator hardware.
